title: Relaxing the clear-sky assumption: Cloud-tolerant spatiotemporal fusion via mask-guided feature modulation and temporal-memory collaboration
summary: The precise characterization of dynamic Earth surface processes relies on time-series remote sensing imagery with both high spatial fidelity and frequent temporal coverage. While spatiotemporal fusion (STF) bridges this resolution trade-off by integrating complementary observations, its practical application remains constrained by the idealized ”clear-sky assumption”. This requirement often favors the selection of temporally distant cloud-free acquisitions over temporally closer but cloud-contaminated observations, potentially reducing the relevance of reference information. To address this limitation, we propose CloudSTF, a robust framework designed to achieve high-fidelity reconstruction by effectively exploiting partially occluded observations. Our approach employs a Mask-guided Multi-scale Swin Transformer (M 2 ST) encoder to capture cloud spatial patterns and suppress noise propagation during feature extraction. This is coupled with a Cross-temporal Memory-guided Fusion (CTMF) module that adaptively integrates temporal trends with textural details retrieved from a spatio-temporal memory bank. To validate this paradigm, we introduce the Global Cloud-shrouded Regions (GCR-STF) benchmark, a geographically distributed dataset comprising 24 representative agricultural and urban sites across six continents. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CloudSTF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Additional assessments across varying cloud densities and diverse landscapes further demonstrate the robustness and applicability of CloudSTF under realistic cloud-contaminated conditions. These results suggest that CloudSTF provides a reliable solution for continuous Earth monitoring in realistic, cloud-prone environments. Source code and the GCR-STF benchmark are available at https://github.com/Sichen-Lu/CloudSTF .

title: Estimating supraglacial lake bottom ablation rates by integrating ICESat-2 repeat track data and multi-temporal sentinel-2 imagery
summary: Supraglacial lakes are widely distributed across the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) each summer. The resulting meltwater-enhanced ablation effect plays a critical role in understanding the GrIS surface mass balance but remains poorly quantified. Inspired by the insight that longer meltwater persistence leads to stronger meltwater-enhanced ablation, this study proposes a novel method to directly estimate supraglacial lake bottom ablation rates at centimeter-per-day scale using satellite observations. First, we map multi-temporal supraglacial lake extents from Sentinel-2 imagery to estimate cumulative meltwater-covered days. Then, we derive ablation depths at the lake bottom and surrounding bare ice by differencing ICESat-2 repeat track data acquired before and during the melt season. Next, we perform linear fitting between lake bottom ablation depths and cumulative meltwater-covered days along the ICESat-2 tracks to calculate both the lake bottom ablation rate and the bare ice ablation rate. Finally, we evaluate the magnitude of the meltwater-enhanced ablation effect. We apply this method to 26 supraglacial lakes across the GrIS and identify a positive linear relationship between lake bottom ablation depths and cumulative water-covered days (mean Pearson correlation coefficient r = 0.70 ± 0.14, p < 0.001). The fitted mean lake bottom ablation rate (4.50 ± 1.15 cm/day) significantly exceeds the mean bare ice ablation rate (1.98 ± 0.52 cm/day). Meltwater in supraglacial lakes therefore enhances ablation rate by ∼ 1.3 ± 0.5 times, with values ranging from 0.6 to 2.4, consistent with previous field measurements (1.1–1.4 times) and numerical model simulations (1.1–1.7 times). In summary, this study provides a first quantitative satellite-based estimate of meltwater-enhanced ablation across the GrIS under varying ablation intensities, and may improve our understanding of GrIS surface melt process.

title: Analysis of intraday urban thermal anisotropy and downward shortwave radiation through UAV experiment and coupled model
summary: The pronounced thermal radiation anisotropy observed in rapidly urbanizing areas arises from the complex interplay of solar downward shortwave radiation (DSWR), building geometry, and local topography. To address this, we propose a novel framework, termed GRay-AU3SM-IRT, for the analysis of urban thermal anisotropy (UTA). The study was conducted in a representative mountainous city in Chongqing, China. A specific 0.4 × 0.4 km 2 area, characterized by buildings and terrain on 10° slopes, was selected for analysis at hourly resolution. The simulations showed strong agreement with measured data, achieving a root mean square error below 0.46 K and a coefficient of determination exceeding 0.79. The analysis reveals that UTA shows pronounced diurnal variations: it intensifies gradually in the morning, peaks at solar noon with clear hotspot formation, and generates secondary hotspots in the afternoon due to changing solar azimuth and slope effects. The morning striped distribution pattern caused by building geometry diminishes with declining solar irradiance and disappears by afternoon. Diurnal trends in the UTA Effect (UTAE), directional brightness temperature (DBT), DBT Effect (DBTE), and DSWR are generally aligned. Notably, UTAE and DBTE peak before DSWR, while both maximum and minimum DBT peak later. The proposed framework offers key advantages: precise multi-lap UAV navigation, minimized motion artifacts, consistent temporal sampling via adaptive velocity control, gap-filling through simulation, and spatio-temporal outlier correction. It provides critical data for angle normalization and correction across diverse urban environments.

title: Remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained reconstruction of 4-hourly chlorophyll-a dynamics in inland lakes using vision Mamba and temporal attention
summary: Chlorophyll a (Chl-a) is widely used to indicate eutrophication and bloom risk in inland waters, but daily Sentinel-3 observations alone cannot resolve transient sub-daily variability represented in partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a records. This study therefore develops VGTA (Vision Mamba–GKOA–TCN-Attention), a staged remote-sensing-assisted and in situ-constrained framework that integrates daily Sentinel-3 OLCI-derived priors with partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences and binary observation masks. A 20-dimensional OLCI-derived feature space provides spectral–spatial priors for Chl-a estimation and bloom-risk state identification. GKOA optimizes TCN-Attention to reconstruct masked values within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences. Vision Mamba outperformed CNN– and Transformer-based models in Chl-a estimation, achieving 94.8% accuracy, a Macro-F1 score of 0.909, and a Bloom-F1 score of 0.870. Ablation experiments confirmed the contributions of bidirectional contextual modeling, positional embedding, selective state-space modeling, and gating. Under Missing Completely at Random, block-missing, and real missing scenarios, GTA improved reconstruction performance by 12.71–55.54% relative to the best baseline models. Uncertainty increased once continuous gaps reached seven days, defining a practical boundary of data-driven reconstruction. Chl-a fluctuations and bloom-risk transitions can unfold within a day, and daily satellite snapshots may blur their timing or miss short events. Reconstruction of masked time steps within partially observed 4-hourly in situ Chl-a sequences can support earlier identification of bloom-risk transitions, more timely field sampling and management responses, and temporally finer monitoring of inland waters.

title: Reference-anchored envelope modelling for predicting tree mortality hotspots driven by drought
summary: Predicting tree mortality hotspots driven by drought remains challenging, since vulnerability to drought is strongly influenced by climate, landform, and substrate. We propose a novel reference-anchored, quantile-envelope susceptibility model-implemented through a reproducible workflow- that exports mortality-resemblance (high-risk) environments from three confirmed tree-mortality footprints (training AOIs), based on semi-arid conifer and evergreen sclerophyllous forests in Cyprus, to produce wide screening layers. The approach combines (i) physiographic similarity derived from AOI-calibrated envelopes for slope, multi-scale topographic position and curvature (broad quantiles; majority-rule), (ii) exposure constraints via circular aspect windows, warm-season solar loading (April-September) and substrate (lithology) filtering, (iii) a drought severity gate (SPEI-12 (Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index-12) ≤ -1.4), and (iv) Landsat event-year spectral collapse relative to a fixed 3-year pre-event baseline, coupled with a year + 1 persistence rule to suppress transient stress. Our within-AOI evaluation (forest-only) showed substantial representativeness (coverage 70.49–85.35%), while recovering most reference mortality pixels (recall 67.62–100%). In 2025, two independent mortality sites were identified in Cyprus, coinciding with exceptional drought (SPEI < -2) and a sharp decline in the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) consistent with foliage browning, and occurring within high-risk zones as mapped in the final risk map. As a plausibility check, both 2025 sites fell within pre-mapped high-risk zones, with 83.50% and 82.69% of their forested area exceeding HEAT ≥ 0.60 and mean risk scores of 84.91% and 75.55%, respectively. With 18.88% of Cyprus’s total forest flagged as high-risk, the probability of this co-occurrence being random is p ≈ 0.036 (binomial test). Anchoring calibration to local mortality footprints makes the approach readily transferable to other regions with documented events.

title: A Targeted–Refined Framework for wind turbine detection integrating AlphaEarth Foundations and high-resolution multispectral satellite imagery
summary: The rapid expansion of clean energy systems, particularly wind and solar power, has made large-scale monitoring of related infrastructure using high-resolution multispectral satellite imagery increasingly important yet challenging. Conventional wind turbine detection approaches rely on pixel-level analysis of high-resolution imagery or sliding-window strategies. These methods often suffer from computational redundancy, low efficiency, and false-positive accumulation, making them inadequate for large-area surveys and operational monitoring. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Targeted–Refined Framework that integrates AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) with high-resolution Jilin-1 imagery. In the Targeted Spatial-Prior Generation Stage, the Unified Spatial Prior Generation Framework (USPGF) is developed to generate high-recall wind turbine candidate regions from AEF land-surface semantic embeddings, thereby replacing exhaustive full-area search with targeted candidate screening. In the Refined Detection Stage, the candidate regions are spatially matched to the corresponding high-resolution Jilin-1 image tiles, which are then processed using a YOLO-based model for refined wind turbine localization. Experimental results showed that fewer than 5 % of the high-resolution image tiles were retained by the Targeted Spatial-Prior Generation Stage, and the proposed framework achieved a recall of 96.85 %, a precision of 98.41 %, and an F1-score of 97.63 % on the Tianjin test set. Furthermore, the proposed Targeted–Refined Framework was directly applied to the Beijing–Hebei (BH) region for cross-regional evaluation. In this evaluation, the framework produced 1,580 detections, including 1,512 true positives and 68 false positives, and achieved an F1-score of 91.39 %, indicating favorable cross-regional generalization performance. Overall, this framework provides an efficient and scalable solution for large-scale detection of spatially sparse objects and offers a practical approach for infrastructure inventory and monitoring of wind farms and similar assets.

title: Multi-angular assessment of early-season defoliation: Evaluating the sensitivity of vegetation indices to NPV visibility in temperate broadleaved forests
summary: Early-season forest decline in temperate broadleaved stands often lacks detectable biochemical stress signals, manifesting primarily through reduced foliage density and increased visibility of non-photosynthetic vegetation (NPV). This study investigated the spectral separability of green leaves and NPV components under varying levels of canopy defoliation. Using a crane platform, we collected in situ leaf- and canopy-level spectrometer measurements alongside co-aligned photography to quantify the visible fraction of NPV. We analyzed the multi-angular reflectance characteristics and evaluated 35 vegetation indices (VIs) —including green biomass metrics and specialized NPV indices —using Random Forest to identify optimal spectral and geometric configurations. Sunlit young foliage exhibited high forward scatter, creating a nadir reflectance minimum. At canopy level, a nadir minimum was driven by the gap distribution resulting from sustainable forest management practices. Consequently, the optimal viewing angle for top-ranking VIs (e.g., SNC BAO , Ctr 2 , mNDVI 705 ) was near the hotspot geometry, minimizing shadowing and forest floor interference. While the total visible fraction of NPV remained mostly insensitive to viewing angles, its shaded proportion varied. VIs targeting green vegetation via red-edge and NIR domains consistently outperformed dedicated NPV indices based on SWIR cellulose and lignin absorption. This is attributed to low upper-canopy SWIR transmittance, which obscured the signals of the largely shaded NPV fraction. Top-performing VIs achieved R 2 = 0.92 for NPV visibility prediction, improving by 21 % over the best SWIR indices and 11 % over the nadir view. To accurately detect initial defoliation and overcome forest floor interference, adopting off-nadir viewing geometries is advantageous for capturing the optimal signal.

title: Unsupervised soft-min fusion of multi-sensor turbidity products using Gaussian mixture models
summary: Turbidity is a key indicator of water quality and particulate dynamics, making its accurate monitoring essential for aquatic ecosystem management. While satellite remote sensing enables large-scale turbidity observation, products derived from different sensors often exhibit inconsistencies due to differences in spectral responses, residual atmospheric effects, and viewing geometries. Effectively integrating such multi-source data in the absence of ground truth remains a significant challenge. Here, we propose Gaussian mixture model-based soft-min (GMMS), a fully unsupervised fusion framework in which neither model construction nor weight estimation relies on ground-truth turbidity observations. GMMS integrates Gaussian mixture modeling with a soft-min weighting strategy to identify latent error-structure contexts and adaptively assign sensor weights according to relative residual stability. By exploiting inter-sensor error characteristics, the framework enables context-aware data fusion. At the overall scale, GMMS significantly outperforms triple collocation (TC) and extended triple collocation for maximized correlation (ETCC) ( p < 0.05). Compared with in situ turbidity observations, GMMS increases the correlation coefficient from 0.798 to 0.841 and reduces the RMSE from 16.849 to 15.921 TU. Site-level evaluations further indicate enhanced robustness and reduced performance variability across monitoring stations. Simulation experiments confirm that GMMS achieves the greatest and most stable performance gains under conditions of moderate-to-high error-structure separability. Overall, GMMS provides an interpretable and transferable unsupervised fusion framework for improving multi-source satellite-derived turbidity estimates in complex riverine environments.

title: Point-Cloud-Native L-Band Augmentation of SWOT KaRIn: Recovering Canopy-Shadowed Dark Water with NISAR
summary: The SWOT mission's Ka-band Radar Interferometer (KaRIn) delivers surface-water observations at 15-25 m resolution but the operational Level-2 Pixel Cloud is known to miss pixels where dense canopy attenuates the specular return, flagging them as dark water. We show that co-registering NISAR L-band geocoded backscatter onto SWOT PIXC recovers dark-water pixels at matched precision. Over the Congo cuvette the augmentation lifts dark-water recall by 11.3 pp; over the Amazon varzea by 17.9 pp. Both gains clear a pre-registered 10 pp kill gate with disjoint 95% bootstrap confidence intervals versus baseline. A joint-shuffle falsifier confirms the gain is from real sensor information, not regularisation. To our knowledge this is the first combined use of NISAR and SWOT reported quantitatively.

title: A source–medium–receiver framework for modeling wind-driven vegetation cooling in urban landscapes
summary: Vegetation cooling in cities is often represented as a local, isotropic effect, although atmospheric processes can redistribute cooling beyond individual vegetation patches. This simplification may overlook the nonlocal and directionally structured nature of cooling propagation. We developed a physics-guided source–medium–receiver (SMR) framework for the Greater Bay Area of China to compare multi-source isotropic connectivity with prevailing-wind-conditioned connectivity. Vegetation-source strength was represented by the VCSI, and parameters estimated from 2021 to 2023 were frozen for an independent 2024 holdout and contrasting monsoon assessments. Cooling connectivity was modeled using a spatially varying distance-decay function, controlled by the wind speed, moisture content, surface albedo, terrain, and directional constraints from prevailing winds. In 2024, isotropic connectivity showed a stronger relationship with LST (r = −0.8069) than wind-conditioned connectivity (r = −0.7780) and local VCSI (r = −0.7757), with the same general ordering across monsoon and built-up receiver assessments. The source-level decay lengths ranged from 0.504 to 0.518 km, whereas the wind-conditioned emergent multi-source persistence increased from 4.13 to 4.88 km, reflecting cumulative field behaviors. Wind-relative decomposition further showed that annual connectivity was distributed across downwind, crosswind, and upwind pathways. These findings indicate that regional vegetation cooling is primarily characterized by distance-mediated, multi-source connectivity, while prevailing-wind direction acts as a scale- and condition-dependent modifier. This shift in perspective provides a physically grounded framework for effective urban climate analysis and precision greening strategies.

title: Reliable Sar oil-spill segmentation for marine monitoring Via self-supervised denoising and lightweight wavelet–state-space modeling
summary: Reliable SAR oil-spill segmentation must simultaneously address image degradation caused by speckle and semantic confusion caused by look-alike dark features, such as low-wind areas, biofilms, and oceanic internal waves. To this end, this paper proposes the OS-AdaAttReNet-WSSNet framework, which decomposes the task into two complementary stages: self-supervised image restoration and supervised oil-spill segmentation. In the first stage, a self-supervised denoising network, AdaAttReNet, is constructed. Without requiring clean reference images, it integrates rotation-equivariant features, channel-spatial attention, and adaptive residual reconstruction to alleviate the effects of speckle on image texture, weak boundaries, and elongated structures. In the second stage, a lightweight wavelet-state-space segmentation network family, WSSNet, is developed. Multi-Scale Split Attention (MSSAtt), the Dynamic Enhanced Residual Wavelet Encoder (DE-RWE), and the Mamba-Enhanced Multi-scale Context Aggregation Upsampler (MEMCAU) are employed for multi-scale feature enhancement, wavelet-domain structural encoding, and long-range contextual fusion, respectively, thereby improving the recognition and boundary localization of irregular oil slicks. On the PALSAR and Sentinel subsets of the SOS dataset, the proposed framework achieves comparable or higher average segmentation performance than recent oil-spill-specific segmentation models. In particular, WSSNet-Tiny, with only 0.27 M parameters, substantially reduces model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive segmentation performance, demonstrating a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off. In addition, experiments on six external data subsets show that the WSSNet series exhibits a certain degree of direct transferability without using target-domain data for training or adaptation. The proposed framework provides a solution for reliable and efficient SAR oil-spill monitoring that balances segmentation accuracy, computational efficiency, and transferability.

title: Global daily joint reconstruction of TROPOMI tropospheric No 2 columns and averaging kernels with temporally aware deep learning
summary: Achieving spatiotemporal consistency in comparisons between satellite tropospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2) retrievals and numerical models or profile-resolving observations depends on the availability of both seamless NO2 vertical columns and their corresponding averaging kernels (AKs). However, cloud cover, aerosols, and solar-zenith-angle constraints frequently invalidate TROPOMI retrievals. Because existing reconstruction studies typically provide NO2 columns in isolation, AK-weighted analyses remain restricted to the original, fragmented observation footprints. Here we develop a temporally aware deep learning framework that jointly reconstructs TROPOMI tropospheric NO2 columns and 34-layer AKs over global land at 0.05° daily resolution from May 2018 to December 2024, with the resulting gap-filled field representing a clear-view, retrieval-consistent column and providing a lower-bound representation under persistent cloud. Because static-feature ML baselines do not explicitly represent photochemical-lifetime, boundary-layer, and transport processes, we introduce a CNN-Temporal-Attention architecture that explicitly encodes 24-hour pre-overpass meteorological dependencies. For AK, a retrieval-specific operator that lacks Vertical Column Density (VCD)-equivalent spatial priors, we exploit inter-layer continuity in vertical sensitivity through a layer-preserving 1D-CNN. Both models achieve ΔR2 ≤ 0.02 across random, temporal, and spatial-block cross-validation, with the AK model reaching a pooled R2 of 0.96; attribution patterns are consistent with the seasonal variation of the NOx photochemical lifetime, and the learned temporal weighting is consistent with cross-day boundary-layer memory, a bimodal boundary-layer cycling, and a ~2-hour upwind transport-related temporal association. Independent validation against 141 Pandora and 29 MAX-DOAS stations supports daily-to-annual accuracy, while AK-smoothed MAX-DOAS and aircraft spiral-profile comparisons support reconstructed AK physical consistency. Reconstructed fields preserve emission-control trends, COVID-19 responses, and biomass-burning signals. Co-delivering VCDs, layer-resolved AKs, and per-pixel uncertainties enables rigorous AK-weighted analysis beyond the original TROPOMI footprint.
